notes.title: Jected - Rivals Has Left Early Access
notes.content:
Ladies and Gentlemen, please start your engines: Jected - Rivals, our turbo-charged racing game, has officially left Early Access! Kudos to our dedicated team and the amazing community that's been with us since day one.

 Heads up, racers: no more updates or support are planned for Jected-Rivals
Huge thanks to our players for fueling our journey through Early Access. Your feedback, and dedication shaped Jected into what it is today.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/2cfac02854dffefbaee3a8c7ad4d50bd034fe2c5.png[/img]

notes.title: Offline Mode Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/9b65c430d8524975fcd5927911301cc737b2eb49.png[/img]
In this patch we're adding a little something to help combat long wait times or to help rivals play with their friends. Offline Mode! Now you'll be able to select Custom Game, allowing you to setup your own events and shows for you to play with your friend list on a whim. Just select Custom Mode, choose the events or shows you want to crash your way through and get started!

Easy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/4d1b2c592eadc78b87531e6065961df9d1fe7e30.png[/img]
We're also dropping all of our work onto Early Access. Meaning you'll get to see and influence the content we're currently working on. All of the new in-progress events will be labelled and you can hop onto the discussions or discord, to let us know what you think! Enjoy!

notes.title: Content Drop #3
notes.content:

notes.title: Update #2 - Progression Update!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/6a6f83ebcd88f2bc8a888a7cba8faa2427e58569.png[/img]

Update #2 is here and with it, one of the most requested features we've had, [b]Progression[/b]! Every show you compete in will offer you the chance to gain some XP, the better you do, the more you get. As you race through the levels you'll unlock an assortment of skins for your four-wheeled carnage causers. we've added a wicked assortment from basic geometric patterns to some more recognisable by the community! Heres a little peak at what to expect;

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/d501c9b3c3b8eb86ab2b084b6f2da55647da5049.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/07a240ea6303987335031b85587fea3ff6f9440d.png[/img]
[b]Patch Notes[/b]
[list]
[*] Added Progression System, Unlocks and Skin customisation,
[*] Various audio adjustments,
[*] Van balance tweaks,
[*] Squad end screen animations - Win the event in style!
[*] Fixed an issue with points in Crash Derbies when crashing into ghost vehicles,
[*] Fixed issues with visual aim assist.
[/list]

Let us know what you think!

notes.title: Update #1 - Squads, Mascots and More!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/30968ecec11fb687c8ebad4741ec17f02ab00af4.png[/img] With update #1 comes our first step towards group play! Now you’ll be able to use our inbuilt friends list, invite and party system to gather 2 of your rivals to become the greatest team to ever eject! Face off against five other teams and work together to smash your way into first place, eliminating one team at a time to take the win. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/7fb42ff830329f051a70e976d72e579ae7a0d945.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/3d10c16302b2b3fa7a97ef36d3aaf72cc313c3ee.png[/img]
Our latest Rival is here! Say hello Charlie Cheaton, the mascot turned rival is here to show you what he can do. While we wouldn’t trust him as far as we could throw him, thanks to his giant head he’s got plenty of padding for any rough landings he may encounter. 
 
Get access to him and help support the development of Jected – Rivals by picking up our Support Pack DLC, today!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/db9f4a15c1a38661081dab621bcd1879c8c7f338.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/31280fda47dc4ca488daba69435a022e7f28798d.png[/img]

To round off this update we’re also dropping another new map; Dynomine! While you’ve had a little while to get used to our other distance jump maps, we’ve got a brand new one heading your way. Dynomine is about leaving your car behind and getting as far as you can before gravity takes control! Use jump pads, updrafts and acrobatics to get the furthest distance or, leave you-shaped marks on the scenery before getting sent home!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/23ef206fbce12234c278b8e188e53294aee70e76.jpg[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/f3a6c29fd7914aac11bb5ede9032515e9332a2f5.jpg[/img]

[b]Patch Notes
[/b]
[list]
[*] Nudge indicator decal fixed, and indicator updated, 
[*] Perfect Nudge indicator updated, 
[*] Vehicles now maintain momentum when switching in mid-air, 
[*] Competitor table position visibility improved, 
[*] Audio settings updated, 
[*] Further updates and improvements to AI racing splines, 
[*] Joining an active round no longer breaks spectator mode, 
[*] Multiple balance passes on several vehicle aspects, 
[*] Changing language options will now change game languages, 
[*] Nitro UI and usability issues resolved, 
[*] Bots now stop driving after the match ends, 
[*] Loadout car being destroyed no longer disqualifies the player, instead they are now able to respawn at the last checkpoint with a full-health car, 
[*] Cars now receive damage correctly from all obstacles, 
[*] Cars no longer spin in place after a collision.
[/list]

[b]Known Issues
[/b][list]
[*] After the intro players will need to click to continue
[/list]

Let us know what you think!

notes.title: Jected EA Development Sprint #1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/39776bb19f78329dc9b379ee7e2f3138b8243eb2.png[/img][list]
[*] [b]Fleshing Out The Progression System[/b]
We've heard the outcry for progression in Jected and we want to address this. While we can't share details and specifics yet, we are looking at moving it up the priority list to start tackling it sooner than our roadmap states. If you've got suggestions for what you'd like to see, we'd love to hear from you!
[*] [b]Party/Squad Clarity and Bug Fixes[/b]
As we continue to work towards partying up with friends and rolling out as a squad visual indication is super important! The last thing you wanna do is t-bone your own teammate.... right? 
[*] [b]Feedback Deep Dive[/b]
Since early access began we've had an awesome amount of feedback, now its time to do something with it. We'll be pulling apart all we've received across multiple platforms and seeing where the community's pain points are and, how we can address them moving forward.
[*] [b]General Bug Fixes[/b]
While we've had a couple of hotfixes in the past we're also looking into vehicles losing in-air momentum, lag when driving and an assortment of other issues outlined on our forums/discord.
[*] [b]New Character Adjustments[/b]
While we don't want to give too much away about our latest addition to the rivals roster, this one is needing a little more time to fix some of his ... appendages.
[*] [b]Further work on Sewer Race[/b]
Wanting to add a little splash to the races, we wanted to take the next one underground as a change of scenery, here's a quick look;
[/list][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/3a87b0bfe654028635b04aea6f007667cdc506ef.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/0c0ac0e604dced9d1dfeb0c04434f080ce37735c.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/36a9e654d8b93bd7a72e9e2609cf8b0c737f5d55.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/79d944a195f1bfcc2855f17f76b58e715de0cbec.png[/img]
[list]
[*] [b]We reworked the perfect nudge indicator [/b]
Nuding is a key part of Jected Rivals and perfect nudges, can be the difference between podium finish, and leaving empty-handed. Because of this, we wanted to add a better visual indicator for perfect nudges beyond on-screen text.
[*] [b]Squads & Party - tags and highlighting other squad members[/b]
[*] [b]Text Chat First Pass[/b]
[*] [b]Progression Progress[/b]
[*] [b]Work on new event: Balloon Ride[/b]
[*] [b]Work on new map: Sewer Race[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Hotfix - early_access.40695
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/57eaf7d64b1ea1f6b566d5dc1891288dbf34963e.png[/img]
Hello everyone!
We just released a small hotfix, this one addresses the problems some players have had trying to find a game.

Previously when searching for a match if you didn't meet the ping requirements for a server, it would simply cancel the queue. Now it'll expand the search and if unable to locate a server, place you in your own lobby. While this may mean you'll face off with bots only from time to time if you're unable to locate a suitable server, we are now monitoring to see where we may need to deploy extra servers.

But, from now onwards everyone will be able to find a game no matter what.

notes.title: Hotfix - early_access.40544
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/57eaf7d64b1ea1f6b566d5dc1891288dbf34963e.png[/img]
Hello everyone!
We just released a small hotfix, to address some of the issues you are experiencing.

This hotfix addresses the following issues:
- Adjusted a problematic spawn point on the Destruction Dish map
- Fixed an issue where cars would often instantly nose dive when going over ramps
- Fixed some problematic spawn locations on Grand Finale
- Slight adjustment to make the canyon section in the Grand Finale have a smoother flow
- Improved on an issue where players would sometimes lose all momentum when switching back to the vehicle mid air
- Fixed an issue with changing audio settings with a controller 
- Fixed the intro camera in Eagle's Nest

We are aware that there are still other things that don't work as expected, and we are currently investigating those.

Some of these known issues:
- Input lag and strange behaviour on collisions with cars
- Some UI/UX issues where the navigation in menus does not work or is not clear
- Targets in Bullseye Charlie sometimes flicker
- Some problems with cars clipping into objects
- Inability for certain people to find a match

notes.title: Early Access Roadmap
notes.content:
A huge thanks to all who've jumped into the game so far! And a big welcome to all those who're going to be competing in the future and to those who've wishlisted to follow the development of Jected - Rivals. We're really excited to see people getting involved in our game and keeping us informed of how your experience has been so far!

Today we wanted to share with you a little glimpse into what's on the road ahead of Jected and you, the player base.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/d6bb5ea0c9cf584270897a1e8410658e0e6e2f57.png[/img]

[b]May Updates[/b]
[list]
[*] Friends List - Access your steam friends in-game
[*] Parties - Add your friends to an in-game group
[*] Squad Mode - Compete in group vs group tournaments. Best team wins.
[*] New Character - Add to your roster with our latest Rival
[*] New Maps - Destroy the competition in brand new places
[/list]

[b]June Updates[/b]
[list]
[*] Leaderboards - See how you stack up vs your rivals on a global scale
[*] New Mode - Test your skills in our latest event
[*] New Car - Pedal to the metal with our latest four wheels of fury
[*] New Maps - Commit more shortcuts to memory in our latest map
[/list]

[b]July Updates[/b]
[list]
[*] Progression First Pass - Progress is key
[*] New Car - Another new set of wheels to add to your garage
[*] New Maps - Crash out on a brand new set of corners
[*] New Mode - Take on your rivals in a fresh event
[/list]

All this and more is heading to Jected - Rivals and, with your help, we hope to make the most of it. So please swing by our discord, the steam forums or our assorted social media channels and let us know what you think of Jected, what you'd like to see more, or less of. Just keep it constructive!

[b]Note;[/b] All of the above is subject to change based on development cycles, timing and community response.

notes.title: Time to get Jected!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/7564110/2cfac02854dffefbaee3a8c7ad4d50bd034fe2c5.png[/img]

[b]Time to get Jected! Adrenaline-pumped Action-Stunt-Racer Gets New Name, Early Access Date and will be Free to Play![/b]
 
Vienna, Austria, April 28th, 2023: Get ready to buckle up and blast off into the wild world of Jected - Rivals, where cars are just the beginning. With its launch on Steam's Early Access program on May 4th, 2023, you'll be able to experience the craziest car-based events you've ever seen. 

"[i]The new game from Vienna-based studio Pow Wow Entertainment is 50% action, 50% racing, 50% flying & crazy stunts, so it's 200% fun![/i]" says gifted mathematician & Head of PR at THQ Nordic, Florian Emmerich. 
 
Think you've got what it takes to be the last one standing in this elimination-style tournament? Then put your foot on the pedal and your finger on the eject button, because in Jected - Rivals, you'll be flying out of your car and into the air like a living bullet. But don't worry, you've got full control of your character as you race across the sky and crash through obstacles, using gadgets and finding secret shortcuts to leave your rivals behind. Choose your character and your cars to become the winner of the 18-player destruction-packed car carnage, and show everyone who's boss in the ultimate Jected - Rivals championship!

The Jected - Rivals Trailer on YouTube: https://youtu.be/XtLmeb2GcSk

Add Jected - Rivals to your wishlist on Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/1366850/

Jected's Rivals is coming to Steam on May 4th, 2023 as a Free To Play game with optional DLC content.

Enjoy & stay tuned!

notes.title: Dev Blog - Sprint #32
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/7957618dc3e6df36309f1d85e2f98b9cc4f6dc28.jpg[/img]

In this sprint we’ve been working on a myriad of different things to help improve First Time User Experience (FTUE), revisiting the structure and design of some of our existing maps, and developing our AI further so they feel more like other players and less like epic-driver-bots-of-doom. 

Our biggest set of priorities in the run-up to Christmas is general stabilization, bug fixing, and getting the game back into the hands of the community to see what you all think of the changes. You’ll be seeing this pop-up a lot in future blog posts as it's super important to us to get you all back into the world of Stuntfest Worldtour ASAP. The same is also said for our server stabilization progress making sure your competitors are where they’re supposed to be … behind you! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/3d786d6b4bb9819311b3c2ab0a2be6968471be0c.png[/img]
Our first-time user experience has gone through a number of significant iterations since the project began, starting as a general game intro in which, you saw yourself approaching the stadium and were tasked with overcoming a number of obstacles to quickly learn the controls and mechanics integral to the Stuntfest gameplay. A lot of the feedback we received about this was that, while fitting, it really didn’t give the user opportunity to really get to grips with skills/gadgets/etc, they'd be using on a regular basis during their playtime, so we’ve made some pretty big changes. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/5959fa729955b486c60600e2b9c1938b09267251.jpg[/img]

First of all, we’ve made the tutorial into an instanced-based event in which you, accompanied by bots, really get a feel for everything you’ll need to use to get the most out of each Stuntshow. We added a splash of slowmo here and there to really give it that epic feeling and made sure the instructions are truly crystal clear for everyone to be able to understand. 

Our programmers have also been hard at work adding some more believability to our bots and increasing the number of different ways they play. In general, our bots tend to follow “splines” we feed them which look a little like this; 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/7ff570f4f0160fefdba79df4a4df4f1e3e4738e7.jpg[/img]

Now, for those of you thinking “What the Heck?!”, let me explain. Recording the data from our developers and such we build a library of these splines based on how they played, the colours represent different states for the AI such as red meaning use nitro, blue meaning use Jetwing, and black meaning drive. The AI turns this information into in-game actions and you see the end result of an AI racing against you. 

It gets way more complicated when you start adding event-to-event variables such as what happens if you slam into them or their car gets wrecked. This is where our programmers are hard at work, adding more splines, allowing the AI to understand the variation better and really expanding what they do on a moment-to-moment basis. 

The more recordings we create, the more varied the bots will get and the better we actually play in those recordings, the better the bots will get as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/5905620a396640fa0e95cd48be119067e61d93ca.png[/img]
If you’ve had a chance to get your mitts on Stuntfest at any point you’ll remember our tracks tend to mesh natural formations and man-made tracks together to create our events and, while this has worked for the most part, we wanted to revisit these structures to see if we could give our maps more of a natural feel while adding an influence of humans, rather than turning it into a construction site full of metal and such. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/40874c68f57cd50acca74d0b503446ee536d9fa1.jpg[/img]

The goal of those changes is to make the tracks more readable and also to give us the opportunity to add more gameplay-impacting obstacles without making the maps look too chaotic.  

This is happening for a number of maps such as Distance Dam and we’re looking into how we can add certain elements to each map to bring more of a theme to each one, making them instantly recognisable from each other stylistically. Additionally, we’ve begun work on the final knockout map and its first blockout. 

We want to make the final race about proving you really are the best this stuntshow has to offer, so you’ll need to combine all the skills and gadgets you’ve employed to get this far to make it past the finish line first and secure the victory. We’ll have more to show coming soon!

notes.title: Dev Blog - Sprint #31
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/4c28567bf19928fd89126546cea7fd53f12a38fe.jpg[/img]

Since Steam Next Fest we here at Pow Wow have been working to refine the  Stuntfest World Tour based on your feedback and the experience we made with the Steam Next Fest. First of all, thank you all for participating in the Next Fest, and special thanks to each and every one of you who filled out the survey as it gives us a more detailed insight into where you, the community, stand in your enjoyment of our game. We’ll also share the results of the survey with you in a separate post. The idea behind this is to a) show you the overall results and also how we interpret your answers.   

Alongside this, we wanted to give you all more of an insight into what's going into Stuntfest’s development behind the scenes and how we’re working on making our game the craziest and most explosive event it can possibly be every time you boot it up! As you will see we want to go also a few steps further and include all of you in the loop on a regular basis. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/669271aa32f205da5c23aa175d45b3391b3edf3d.png[/img]
To help give you all an understanding of how we work, I need to first explain to you how we divide and conquer. In the big picture, while we’re all one big team working on delivering a single game, we actually work in smaller sections so each group can tackle an area at a time so, in no particular order, these are our teams; 
 
[b]Game Mode [/b]
This crew is in charge of the different game modes you see in the game (duh!). Every event you’ve competed in is their brainchild. From the races to the target range and beyond, these all started and ended with Game Mode. This team mainly consists of designers but also programmers who support on developing mode rules and level design elements (eg. Jump pads) 

[b]Meta[/b] 
The Menus, UI, servers and beyond! All the bits that bring everything and everyone together is handled by Meta. Making sure you know how much nitro you have left, being able to get from the hub to the garage, seeing the leader board between each event? All Meta.  

[b]3C – Character, Control, Camera. [/b]
This one kinda says it on the tin but these are the people who create the characters, the cars, and the bits in-between. AI and net code and physics. All comes down to the 3C team. How the game knew you wrapped your car around the post? Because 3C told it. 

[b]Sprints [/b]
Our teams work in so-called sprints, which are (in our case) 2 week increments in which we commit to certain sprint goals, and after each sprint we assess the results together. In the future we want to give you an overview on what we are planning at the beginning of each sprint and how it went. 

Now you know the teams and how we work, we’ll get right to the point. Speaking of which, let’s find out what they’ve been up to this sprint.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/da3ba69989d225779f8fce4234af0e61c2277a39.png[/img]
This week Game Mode are focused on bringing back the Mini Map with a fresh coat of paint and testing some of the new events in the pipeline, more of which we’ll share in a later dev blog. Reason for removing it for the Steam Next Fest were some performance implications caused by the minimap. They’re also taking the time to clean up several aspects of already existing maps, specifically when it comes to the collectible vehicles which are dotted around. Alongside this, they’re also taking some time to balance the metrics of Crash Derby and Distance Jumps event.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/4961427245748a79bc63ac4d1bc18631b8bf5888.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/bacee92d9f641e008217d32583e97ebe8cf30482.png[/img]
The Meta Team is coming out swinging this sprint with an overhauled menu system, boasting a new style as well as better controller input/navigation along with improvements to the UI and dedicated servers in terms of performance. They’ve also been hard at work with the lore team defining some crucial aspects of our characters and the vehicles from a story standpoint, meaning you may be able to learn more about the competitors and our four-wheeled furies soon! Finally, for those who took part in Steam Next Fest, we should hopefully have a resolution to the pesky failure-to-eject bug in the very near future. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/8d3bee5d02bd008b95eded49dc786a03b1d7a460.png[/img]
3C have been hard at work this sprint with a whole host of improvements to a huge number of things, this includes vehicle collision and netcode, performance and stability, VFX optimisation and AI. Not only are they making sure to improve the overall user experience for both first time and returning players but, they’re putting the pieces together for some new faces and maybe even a new set of wheels.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/ba2c2df711fa8f5d3df2d67784b8e3764b776b0b.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/c2eedb38c4258eadc952c392f0194f277e9b37b2.png[/img]
We can’t thank the Stuntfest Community enough for your support so far! Steam Nextfest was an absolute blast thanks to you all, it was great to see people challenging each other all across the discord and I had a great time wrecking with the best over the wheels worth of live streams we had.

notes.title: Summer of Stunts Feedback
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/SUyRV2q.jpg[/img]

Now that Gamescom is out of the way it's time to catch you up with everything that’s going on in the Pow Wow Entertainment offices. We gathered a whole load of feedback from the Summer of Stunts playtests and it's been a huge help in highlighting areas we need to improve on, we wanted to share some details of what we found with you, the community.
 
First off we wanted to take a moment to thank all of you who turned up, got involved, and most importantly, let us know what you think. For the most part, it was hugely constructive and, you’ve given us a perfect jumping-off point as we head towards our next playtest. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/2da161a6afcceea1585fab8813f6f5d1adb9c8e1.png[/img]

One of the biggest bits of feedback we got was vehicle handling. While Stuntfest is not a racing game at heart, our cars provide a foundation for the game and really need to be something players can jump into and instantly enjoy, while building a preference for certain cars that fit their playstyle. As of Summer of Stunts, this wasn’t the case. Many of you raised the issue of under-steering, uncontrollable drift, and more. That’s why we are tackling both the balancing of the vehicles and also adding some missing functionalities, make sure to keep up with our dev blogs and Q&A’s for a deeper look at our four-wheeled friends. 

Now, there isn’t a perfect science to balancing car controls, it becomes even more complicated when we want to straddle the line between arcade-like pick-up-and-play driving while also having a certain nuance to go from good to God-like behind the wheel. It’s going to take us some time to find the sweet spot but, with your help between playtests, we can refine this until we get there.  Our supercar has already come along hugely since the playtest and we’re excited to show you the others soon. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/1ed7989b67f0784bb492cabb12957c7a6a498cbc.png[/img]

In a similar vein to what's being covered above is the crashing. Multiple parts of feedback expressed how the crashing didn’t feel satisfying, the cars didn’t deform correctly and how in certain events, crashing wouldn’t be detected or, would be detected even if you didn’t hit anyone.  

To begin with we’re hard at work reworking multiple elements of how the cars are damaged and destroyed. This includes working on how collisions are tracked to make them more accurate, making some flappy parts to enhance the look of the deformation and down the line will touch on realism and improve the sounds for that extra audio crunch! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/abeb6e52f690db1cc90e431326122a2ce729c934.png[/img]

The learning experience was something we found players struggled with. With Stuntfest World Tour being unlike anything else out there, it's important to us you’re able to pick up and play within minutes of getting in the game, and currently, our tutorial isn’t quite instructive enough to allow for that. Many players struggled to get to grips with how to eject, use gadgets and resummon their car. It’s of course a lot of different controls that our players need to learn to be competitive in the stuntshow and as every game mode requires you to play a bit differently that amplifies the challenge. With a new tutorial and extended playgrounds in the HUB we hope players will arrive with a stronger knowledge before hopping into a stuntshow.  

First impressions are important and with this in mind, we’re re-working the user experience when you first start the game. Making it more obvious, more engaging, and repeatable in case you’re ever in need of a refresher course. We also hear you about the ability to customize your experience and, while we have no details on that yet, we’re working hard on making it a reality. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/a8e4dafbc7f844166c3f07df221a3c072a308d33.png[/img]

We’re reworking our lighting systems and beyond to, pardon the pun, show Stuntfest in the best light will still trying to match our vision for what we want you to experience. This means going over all our textures and materials to make sure everything fits. While we want to get across the “extreme” elements of Stuntfest, we want to make sure we don’t stray too far into a cartoon dynamic.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/13931bf55d64425ef273438da0c0ece8c1b10d11.png[/img]

All of the above focuses on some key issues you highlighted and, what we’re doing to resolve them. While I’ve not covered everything, we are well aware of the bugs, the issues and the shortcomings and are doing what we can to resolve them. From random/no points during destruction derbies, people leaving lobbies early, and lack of the ability to group, these are all on our laundry list of things to resolve. If you were an early leaver, let us know why, the more information we have the better we can make the experience! 

We’ll be doing our best to keep communicating with you, our budding community, on what we’re fixing, when we’re fixing it and how we’re going to fix it at regular intervals. Alongside this we’re also hosting regular private playtests which you can hear all about on discord, and even discuss the game and what you’d like to see directly with us! 
 
So, from all of us at Pow Wow Entertainment, thank you for the feedback and we look forward to showing you the changes we’ve made, very soon.

notes.title: Dev Blog #1
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/6b9f5edb24bea6b292ff665abe02c89d849e6c44.png[/img]

A huge hello to all you new festival-goers and welcome to our very first dev blog. In hopes to be more transparent with the development process, we wanted to share with you a regular insight into our production process and what we’ve got going on between each development cycle. 

We’ll be talking about the inspiration behind our characters and vehicles, how all the mechanics work, and, how to use them to get ahead of your competition. Alongside this, we hope to show you work-in-progress images and clips from the game, improvements from cycle to cycle, and, maybe even the odd bug to show what happens when physics stops working!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/2018ec9201351ad0e0a671ec28805272c82db4af.png[/img]

Ever since our reveal trailer in July, we’ve been getting this question a lot on our social media channels in video comments. In our very first blog, it may be time we spent a moment to straighten things out and explain exactly what Stuntfest is all about!

Stuntfest Worldtour is breaking the mould by combining driving, gadgets, stunts and a knockout tournament all within the space of 30 minutes! Using a weird, wacky and downright wonderful set of tools you can catapult yourself from the driver's seat and into the skies. Gliders, jetpacks, grappling hooks, and more allow you to set yourself out from the other races and allow you to take advantage of all sorts of shortcuts and acrobatic routes to steal the lead.

We’ve already found ourselves compared to multiple other racing games out right now and we want to make it clear that our hybrid gameplay takes us off the track way more than we stay on it. While we may have destruction derbies, lap-based races, and other track shenanigans, Stuntfest is way more than that and our Stuntshows are just the tip of the iceberg.

18 enter, but only one can emerge victorious! The main activity in Stuntfest Worldtour is our Stuntshows, a gathering of 18 players who battle it out across multiple connected events from lap-based races, length & height-based ejection events, glider sprints, and a few more extravagant exhibitions. After each event, your success (or spectacular failure) is awarded points, didn’t get enough points to stay in the green? Bye-bye. Try again next time.

If you’re fast enough and badass enough, you might find yourself the stunt show winner, and if that’s the case, you get to show off in front of the rest of the fest, by leaping back into our hub in style! But, it’s not all about being able to keep all 4 wheels on the track, sometimes it's about leaving your car behind altogether.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42594143/9ec74053a44a2d28519cef42bdfcbb80a33ee48e.png[/img]

Going forward we at Pow Wow Entertainment want to be as transparent as possible with our plans, development process, and ideas behind the features and mechanics within Stuntfest. We’ll revisit the Stuntshow to talk in-depth about the highs and the lows of the event as a whole. We’ve got plans to show off all the cars and characters and their unique characteristics, how they went from concept art to playable entities, and how the world of Stuntshow Worldtour itself came to be.

Alongside all these we’ll be having weekly Twitch streams, posting daily content and Stuntfest advice across multiple social media platforms and holding daily chats on our discord to make sure you can keep up-to-date and informed on Stuntfest and its production.

Through the coming months we’re going to be looking to you, our community, to help make Stuntfest a truly unique experience and are constantly looking for input and feedback. With your involvement we can take Stuntfest from something we want to make, to something you want to play!

Make sure to wishlist here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1366850/Stuntfest__World_Tour/

Thanks for taking the time to catch up with us, Festival-goers. We’ll see you next time!

Enjoy & Stay tuned!
